newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WE'RE NOT AFRAID OF ENGLISH, SAYS DORTMUND COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WE'RE NOT AFRAID OF ENGLISH, SAYS DORTMUND COACH.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld is confident that his team can beat Manchester United in next month's European Cup semifinals and said Friday's draw for the venues of the legs was irrelevant.
Dortmund were drawn to play the first leg on April 9 in Germany before travelling to England for the decisive return leg at Old Trafford two weeks later.

But Hitzfeld said: "It doesn't matter at all whether we play at home or away in the first leg. We're just as strong away from home as at home. Our game in Auxerre proved that. We're not afraid of English football."
Dortmund won both legs of their quarter-final against French side Auxerre, taking the first match in Germany 3-1 and the second leg in France 1-0.
Club chairman Gerd Niebaum said Friday's draw was perfect for the German champions.

"I wanted a set-up like that because we have had good experience with it in the past," Niebaum said. "We can set up the foundations for a place in the final in the first leg. We are unbeaten away from home in the Champions' League this season."
